questions.question: Which of the following personality is associated with Aligarh movement?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** **__**Syed Ahmed Khan.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Syed Ahmed Khan** is associated with the Aligarh movement, which was a **socio-religious reform movement in the 19th century** aimed at uplifting the Muslim community in India.
 
• **Syed Ahmed Khan was a prominent Muslim reformer and educationist** who believed that education was the key to the progress and empowerment of the Muslim community.
 
• He founded the** Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College in Aligarh,** which later became Aligarh Muslim University, to provide modern education to Muslims and to promote communal harmony.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Muhammad Ali Jinnah, Abul Kalam Azad, and Syed Amir Ali **were also prominent Muslim leaders and reformers, but they were associated with different movements and ideologies.
 
• ** Muhammad Ali Jinnah was a leader of the All-India Muslim League** and played a key role in the partition of India and the creation of Pakistan.
 
• ** Abul Kalam Azad was a nationalist Muslim** leader who opposed the idea of partition and worked for Hindu-Muslim unity.
 
• ** Syed Amir Ali was a lawyer and politician** who was associated with the Indian National Congress and worked for the rights of Muslims in India.**.**

questions.question: Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) was started in which year?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** 2015.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• **This is the correct answer as PMKVY was launched in 2015.**
 
• ** Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) **is a skill development scheme launched by the** Government of India in 2015.**
 
• The scheme aims to provide **training and certification to Indian youth in various industries and sectors to improve their employability and productivity.**
 
• The **National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC)** implements the scheme **under the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship.**
 
• PMKVY offers monetary rewards and placement assistance to **eligible candidates who successfully complete the training program. **

**​** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Other Important Schemes:**

 
• **Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY):**

 
 
• PMUY was launched by Prime Minister of India Narendra Modi on 1 May 2016 to distribute 50 million LPG connections to women of Below Poverty Line (BPL) families.
 
• A budgetary provision of ₹ 80 billion (US$1.0 billion) was made for the scheme.
 
• The program's goal was expanded over time to provide LPG connections to eight crore women by March 2020.
 
• This scheme was replaced by the Ujjwala Yojana 2.0 in 2021.
 
• Ujjwala 2.0 offers beneficiaries a deposit-free LPG connection along with a free first refill and hotplate.
 
 
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY):**
 
 
• Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY) was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in June 2015.
 
• The main objective of this scheme is to provide housing for all by the year 2022.
 
• PMAY aims to build 2 crore houses for the urban and rural poor.
 
• The scheme aims to provide affordable houses with water facilities, sanitation, and electricity supply round-the-clock.
 
• Two major segments of PMAY are Urban ('PMAY-U') and Gramin ('PMAY-G') focusing on urban and rural poor respectively.

questions.question: Gautama Buddha attained enlightenment under a peepal tree at _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Bodh Gaya. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gautama Buddha **attained** enlightenment **under a **peepal tree at Bodh Gaya, **which is located in the Indian state of** Bihar.**
 
• The peepal tree under which Buddha attained enlightenment is also known as the **Bodhi Tree, **which is considered **sacred by Buddhists.**
 
• **Bodh Gaya is home to the Mahabodhi Temple, **which was built by** Emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE** to commemorate Buddha's enlightenment
 
• **The Mahabodhi Temple complex **also** includes the Vajrasana,** which is believed to be the spot where Buddha meditated and attained enlightenment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Important events in the life of Gautama Buddha:**

 
• The Buddha, initially known as **Siddhartha Gautama,** was born into a royal family in **Lumbini,** currently located in **Nepal, in the 6th to 4th century BCE.**
 
• At the age of 29, after witnessing the sufferings of life (old age, sickness, death), Gautama renounced his royal life in **search of the path to end human suffering.**
 
• For several years, he embraced the life of an ascetic, practicing extreme austerity. However, he found this didn't lead to enlightenment and instead advocated for what he called** "the Middle Way"**—a life of moderation away from extreme asceticism and hedonism.
 
• After attaining enlightenment, the Buddha delivered his **first sermon in Sarnath**, near **Varanasi in India**, often referred to as **"Setting the Wheel of Dhamma in Motion**". It marked the beginning of his teaching or the dissemination of his understanding of the "truth" about life and existence.
 
• Buddha initiated a community of followers, both **monks (Bhikkus) and nuns (Bhikkunis).** This Buddhist monastic community, known as Sangha, spread the teachings of Buddha after his death.
 
• The Buddha died at the **age of 80, in Kushinagar, India.** His death is also termed as** Parinirvana, **the final Nirvana. After his death, the Buddha's teachings were collected into written form, called **Tripitaka (Three Baskets),** forming the foundation of Buddhist philosophy and practice.

questions.question: The Kandariya Mahadeva Temple was constructed in 999 A.D. by the king Dhangadeva of ___________ dynasty.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chandela.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Kandariya Mahadeva Temple** was constructed by** King Dhangadeva of the Chandela dynasty in 999 A.D.**
 
• **The Chandela dynasty** ruled in central India from the **9th to the 13th century **and was known for their patronage of art and architecture, particularly the erotic sculptures on their temples.
 
• It's **part of the Khajuraho Group of Monuments**, a UNESCO World Heritage site, located in **Madhya Pradesh, Central India.**
 
• The Chandela dynasty was known for its art and architecture, and **among their 85 original temples, around 22 survive today **and reflect the height of the North Indian art form known as** 'Nagara'.**
 
• The Kandariya Mahadeva Temple is **dedicated to Lord Shiva **and houses a linga in the main shrine.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Pala dynasty** was a ruling dynasty in eastern India from the 8th to the 12th century, known for their patronage of Buddhism and the Nalanda University.
 
• **The Pallava dynasty** was a ruling dynasty in southern India from the 3rd to the 9th century, known for their patronage of art, literature, and architecture, particularly the Shore Temple in Mahabalipuram.
 
• **The Chola dynasty** was a ruling dynasty in southern India from the 9th to the 13th century, known for their naval power, trade, and patronage of art and architecture, particularly the Brihadeeswara Temple in Thanjavur.

questions.question: Which was the first ancient Indian civilization that had systematic town planning and underground drainage systems?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Indus Valley civilization.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Indus Valley civilization is one of the earliest civilizations in the world and flourished around 2600 BCE.**
 
• The Indus Valley civilization was notable for its advanced town planning**, which included well-organized streets, drainage systems, and public buildings.**
 
• The ancient cities of Harappa and Mohenjo-Daro in the Indus Valley region had well-planned streets, public baths, and underground drainage systems ahead of their time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Early Nubian civilization** refers to the civilization that emerged in the **Nile Valley around 2000 BCE.** Still, there is no evidence of systematic town planning or underground drainage systems in this civilization.
 
• **Later Vedic civilization **refers to the period of Indian history tha**t followed the decline of the Indus Valley civilization,** and while this period saw the emergence of the caste system and the Vedas, there is no evidence of systematic town planning or underground drainage systems.
 
• **Aegean civilization** refers to the civilizations that emerged in the Aegean region, including the Minoan and Mycenaean civilizations, but while these civilizations had impressive art and architecture, there is no evidence of systematic town planning or underground drainage systems.

questions.question: Which of the following layers of the atmosphere means "region of mixing"?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Troposphere.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The lowermost layer of the atmosphere with an average height of 13 km (16 km over the equator and 6 km over the poles).
 
• The air we breathe exists here. Almost all the weather phenomena (like rainfall, fog, clouds, dew, frost and hailstorm) occur in this layer.
 
• Temperature decreases with increasing height at the rate of 6.5℃ per 1000m. This is called normal lapse rate.
 
• The height of the troposphere varies from the equator towards the pole (decreases towards the poles) and from one season to another (increases during summer while decreases during winter) during a year.
 
• The upper limit is called the tropopause which is 1.5 km thick. (The word “troposphere” literally means “zone/region of mixing” and tropopause menas “where the mixing stops”.)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

Stratosphere

 
• Above the troposphere lies the stratosphere. It extends up to a height of 50 km.
 
• This layer is almost free from clouds and associated weather phenomena, making conditions most ideal for flying aeroplanes.
 
• One important feature of the stratosphere is that it contains a layer of ozone gas between the height of 15 to 30 km (also called Ozonosphere).
 
• Temperature increases with height due to the absorption of UV rays by the ozone layer.
 
• The upper limit of the stratosphere is known as stratopause.

Mesosphere

 
• Lying above the stratosphere this is the third layer of the atmosphere and extends between 50 km and 80 km.
 
• Meteorites burn up in this layer on entering from space.
 
• Temperature decreases with increasing height again.
 
• The uppermost limit is the mesopause where the temperature becomes -80℃.

Ozone Layer

 
• The ozone layer is an area or a continuous region in the stratosphere of the earth that includes high concentrations of ozone(O₃) and protects the earth from the sun's harmful ultraviolet radiation.

Thermosphere

 
• Temperature here rises very rapidly with increasing height.
 
• The International Space Station is situated in this layer.
 
• It is further divided into two layers:

Ionosphere:

 
• It extends between 80 - 400 km.
 
• This layer helps in radio transmission. In fact, radio waves transmitted from the earth are reflected back to the earth by this layer.
 
• Includes a number of ionic layers with increasing heights like the D layer, E layer, F layer and G layer.

questions.question: The GDP estimation method measuring the aggregate value of factor payments is called ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**income method.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The income method is one of the** three methods used to estimate a country's Gross Domestic Product (GDP), the other two being the expenditure method and the production or value-added method.**** **
 
• The income method measures the** total income earned by all factors of production in a country, including wages, salaries, profits, and rent.**
 
• The income method is also known as the factor income approach because it calculates the GDP by adding up the income earned by all the factors of production involved in producing goods and services.
 
• The income method is particularly useful for measuring the GDP of countries where most economic activity is in the form of services rather than goods production.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The product method calculates GDP, which measures the total value of goods and services produced in a country over a certain period.**
 
• The value-added method is a method of calculating** GDP that measures the value added at each stage of production in a country.**

questions.question: In India, the practice of erecting megaliths began about ___________ ago.
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

• **The practice of erecting megaliths began in India about 3000 years ago.**
 
• Megaliths are large stones used to **construct monuments or structures.**
 
• The megalithic culture in India is said to have originated in the** Deccan Plateau and spread to other regions.**
 
• Megaliths were used for various purposes such as** burial chambers, memorials, and astronomical observatories.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• The term megalith is derived from the Greek word 'megas' which means great and 'lithos' meaning stone.
 
• The stone boulders are known as megaliths (literally big stones).
 
• These were carefully arranged by people and were used to mark burial sites.
 
• The practice of erecting megaliths began about 3000 years ago, and was prevalent throughout the Deccan, south India, in the north-east and Kashmir.

questions.question: Which among the following team won the International Cricket Council (ICC) Men's T20 World Cup 2021?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Australia.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• **Australia defeated New Zealand** in the final to win the** ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2021.**
 
• This was** Australia's first win in an ICC Men's T20 World Cup.**
 
• **Mitchell Marsh**, from the Australian team, was awarded **"Player of the Match"** in the final for his **outstanding batting performance.**
 
• The Men's T20 World Cup 2021 was held in the **United Arab Emirates and Oman.**
 
• The win was viewed as a major achievement for Australian cricket, further establishing their supremacy in international cricket across different formats.

questions.question: "Wide Angle" is an autobiography of which of the following sportsperson?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Anil Kumble.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• **"Wide Angle" is an autobiography written by Anil Kumble himself.**
 
• Anil Kumble is a** former Indian cricketer and a former captain of the Indian cricket team.**
 
• He was one of the **best spin bowlers in the world and is known for his accuracy and consistency.**
 
• Kumble is also the third-highest wicket-taker in Test cricket and the only Indian bowler to take all ten wickets in a Test innings.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Wasim Akram** is a former Pakistani cricketer and one of the greatest fast bowlers in the history of cricket.

 
 
• He has also written an autobiography named** "Wounded Tiger".**
 
 
 
• **Yuvraj Singh **is a former Indian cricketer and a left-handed all-rounder.
 
 
• The Test of my Life is an Autobiography of Yuvraj Singh.
 
 
 
• ** Imran Khan **is a former Pakistani cricketer and the current Prime Minister of Pakistan.
 
 
• He has written an autobiography named "All Round View".

questions.question: Which religious group of people celebrates the Nowruz festival in India ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** **__**Parsis.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• **Nowruz is a festival that marks the Persian New Year and is celebrated by Parsi communities in India.**
 
• Parsis are followers of the **Zoroastrian religion, which originated in ancient Persia (modern-day Iran) and was brought to India by Persian immigrants.** 
 
• The festival usually falls on or around **March 21st and is celebrated with feasting, dancing, and the exchange of gifts.**
 
• Nowruz is also celebrated in other countries with significant Persian and Zoroastrian populations, such as Iran, Afghanistan, and Tajikistan. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Jews celebrate Hanukkah, Passover, and other religious holidays. 
 
• Buddhists celebrate Vesak, the birthday of Buddha, as well as other festivals specific to different Buddhist traditions.
 
• Jains celebrate Mahavir Jayanti, the birth anniversary of the founder of Jainism, as well as other important dates in the Jain calendar.
